AdvisoryItemModel.description: One thing worth a human's attention that changes no verdict.

at_seq.description: Where, when the item has a location.
at_seq.title: At Seq

boot_id.description: Hex boot identifier, when scoped to one.
boot_id.title: Boot Id

detail.description: The package's description of this item.
detail.title: Detail

AdvisoryItemModel.title: AdvisoryItemModel

AdvisoryModel.description: The advisory channel, carried apart from the verdict on purpose.

note.default: advisory items do not affect the verdict
note.description: Carried in the payload rather than left to the UI. A consumer that receives advisory items beside chain_ok will eventually treat them as part of it.
note.title: Note

AdvisoryModel.title: AdvisoryModel

AnchorAttemptModel.description: One source that was consulted, and what came back.

outcome.description: 'answered', 'absent' or 'error'. Three states, never two: absent is normal, error is a source that exists and could not be read, and merging them would hide a corrupt anchor file behind 'no anchor configured'.
outcome.title: Outcome

source_detail.description: Which one — a path, or free text.
source_detail.title: Source Detail

AnchorAttemptModel.title: AnchorAttemptModel

AnchorCadenceModel.description:
How often this boot anchored its head.

The widest gap is the useful figure: it is how long the chain went
without an external witness, and therefore how wide an "existed by"
bracket would be for records inside it.

count.description: Anchor records written during this boot.
count.title: Count

widest_gap_ns.description: Longest interval between anchors, in nanoseconds.
widest_gap_ns.title: Widest Gap Ns

AnchorCadenceModel.title: AnchorCadenceModel

AnchorProfile.description:
An ordered list of places to look for a trusted head.

Order is meaningful and is the user's: the first source that answers wins,
and the ones before it are reported as tried. That is why resolution is
availability-first — a source that errors does not stop the walk — and why
the provenance view has to show what was skipped rather than only what
answered.

name.description: Profile name, used as the verify parameter.
name.title: Name

sources.description: Tried in order; the first that answers is used.
sources.title: Sources

AnchorProfile.title: AnchorProfile

AnchorReadingModel.description: The head that answered, and where it came from.

head.description: The hex head this check was made against.
head.title: Head

AnchorReadingModel.title: AnchorReadingModel

AnchorSourceSpec.description:
One place a trusted head might live.

The shell owns the concrete sources; the package owns what a head means
(L2). A spec is therefore plain data — no package type appears in a
request model.

account.description: For kind='keychain': the account name the head is stored under. The service name is fixed by the application, so this is the only part an operator chooses.
account.title: Account

detail.description: Free text shown beside this source in the provenance view.
detail.title: Detail

head.description: For kind='manual': the 64-character hex head, as handed over.
head.title: Head

module_path.description: For kind='pkcs11': path to the PKCS#11 module the token speaks through (a .so, .dylib or .dll).
module_path.title: Module Path

object_label.description: For kind='pkcs11': the label of the data object on the token. Omitted means the package's own default, 'pala-anchor-head'.
object_label.title: Object Label

path.description: For kind='file': path to a FileAnchor head file.
path.title: Path

pin_account.description: For kind='pkcs11': the keychain account holding the token's user PIN. Required, and a keychain account rather than the PIN itself: profiles are returned in full by GET /anchors/profiles, so a PIN carried here would be readable by anyone holding the session token. Required because a head the package itself writes is invisible to a session without one, and would read as absent while present.
pin_account.title: Pin Account

token_label.description: For kind='pkcs11': the label of the token holding the head.
token_label.title: Token Label

AnchorSourceSpec.title: AnchorSourceSpec

AnchorStore.description: Where this installation keeps its anchor profiles.

path.description: The profiles file, or null when kept in memory only.
path.title: Path

problem.description: Why the file could not be read, or null. While set, the file is left as it is and every change to a profile is refused.
problem.title: Problem

AnchorStore.title: AnchorStore

BootBoundary.description:
Where one boot begins and ends, on both axes.

Rendered as an axis break rather than a seam (§C-03). `monotonic_ns`
resets across a boot, so no duration spans one — and nothing in this
payload computes one that does.

first_wall_ns.description: Wall clock at its first record.
first_wall_ns.title: First Wall Ns

last_wall_ns.description: Wall clock at its last record.
last_wall_ns.title: Last Wall Ns

BootBoundary.title: BootBoundary

BootView.description:
One boot, with the statistics the package computes for it.

A boot is the unit that matters for reading time: `monotonic_ns` resets
across a boundary, so no duration spans one.

recovery_seq.description: Where this boot recovered a truncated tail, when it did. Null is the ordinary case rather than a missing value.
recovery_seq.title: Recovery Seq

time_trust_values.description: Every wall-clock trust level seen inside this boot. More than one means the clock changed status mid-boot, which qualifies every wall-time claim in it — so the set is carried rather than reduced to the latest.
time_trust_values.title: Time Trust Values

uptime_ns.description: Monotonic span of this boot, computed by the package.
uptime_ns.title: Uptime Ns

BootView.title: BootView

ChainResult.description:
Question one, first half: do these records link to each other?

Always answerable. It needs no key and no anchor — only the bytes in
front of it — which is why it is the one question a chain can never
decline to answer.

**It is a header walk.** Whether each record still *is* the bytes its
header claims is a separate question, answered by
:class:`ContainerCheck`. A consumer that renders `chain_ok` alone will
show a sound file when a body has been swapped.

breaks.description: Sequence numbers where prev_hash does not name the predecessor.
breaks.title: Breaks

chain_ok.description: Whether every record header links to its predecessor. Headers only — see ContainerCheck.body_digest_mismatches for whether the bodies still match their digests.
chain_ok.title: Chain Ok

gaps.description: Skipped sequence numbers. A gap is a break whether or not the hashes on either side happen to link.
gaps.title: Gaps

head.description: Hex digest of the last record in the chain.
head.title: Head

uninterpretable.description: Records with an unknown format version or record type. Chain-checked and reported, never rejected — the verifier not understanding a record is not the same as the record being wrong.
uninterpretable.title: Uninterpretable

violation_codes.description: (seq, code) pairs, parallel to `violations` (U24, palimpsests 0.14). The CODE is what a consumer branches on — an open vocabulary (as of 0.14: prefix_absent, genesis_not_first, genesis_prev_hash_nonzero, header_len_mismatch, malformed_tlv, time_trust_undefined, time_unknown_with_wall_clock, empty_body_digest_nonzero, nonempty_body_digest_zero, encrypted_body_too_short); the reason in `violations` is the verifier's sentence, never parsed.
violation_codes.title: Violation Codes

violations.description: (seq, reason) pairs for normative MUSTs the record broke. Kept as pairs: a seq without its reason is a number nobody can act on.
violations.title: Violations

ChainResult.title: ChainResult

ChainSubject.description:
What the container *is*, stated before any verdict about it.

Separate from the verification result on purpose: a reader of a report
must be able to confirm they are holding the same artifact the check ran
against, independently of whether that check passed.

assurance_tiers.description: Every assurance tier the chain's records carry, not just the latest. More than one means the platform guarantee changed mid-chain, and the verdict wording cannot then be a single sentence — so the set is reported rather than reduced.
assurance_tiers.title: Assurance Tiers

bytes.description: File size on disk, in bytes.
bytes.title: Bytes

filename.description: The file's name, for display only.
filename.title: Filename

records.description: Number of records the reader found.
records.title: Records

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file as opened. Identifies the artifact; a report naming only a filename identifies nothing.
sha256.title: Sha256

time_trust_values.description: Every wall-clock trust level the chain's records carry. More than one means the writer's clock changed status mid-chain, which qualifies every wall-time claim in the file.
time_trust_values.title: Time Trust Values

ChainSubject.title: ChainSubject

Completeness.description:
Question two: is what I hold all of it?

The only question that can go unasked, and the answer must say so.

anchor_lag.description: Records present beyond the anchored head, when there are any.
anchor_lag.title: Anchor Lag

anchor_reason.description: The verifier's sentence explaining an incomplete answer.
anchor_reason.title: Anchor Reason

complete_to_anchor.description: True, False, or null. Null means NO ANCHOR ANSWERED — either none was configured, or every source in the profile was absent — so the question was never asked. It is not a pass and must never be rendered as one.
complete_to_anchor.title: Complete To Anchor

Completeness.title: Completeness

ConsistencyCheckView.description: A proof someone holds, against this chain. Three answers, apart.

first_root_matches.description: This chain's root over its first `first` records is the proof's `first_root`: the prefix it names is intact here. Null when this chain holds fewer records.
first_root_matches.title: First Root Matches

path_verifies.description: Its path connects its own two roots — says nothing of where they came from.
path_verifies.title: Path Verifies

second_root_matches.description: The same at `second`; null when this chain holds fewer records.
second_root_matches.title: Second Root Matches

ConsistencyCheckView.title: ConsistencyCheckView

ConsistencyProofView.description: A prefix-consistency proof, as the package made it (E-07, channel 3).

proof.description: `pala-consistency-proof/1`, the package's `to_json()`: counts, the two derived roots, the RFC 6962 path. Derived and unsigned; it re-verifies from the spec alone.
proof.title: Proof

verifies.description: The path connects the two roots (`verify()`).
verifies.title: Verifies

ConsistencyProofView.title: ConsistencyProofView

ContainerCheck.description:
Whether each record is the bytes its own header claims.

A different question from the one `ChainResult` answers. The chain is
about how records link to each other; this is about whether a record's
body still hashes to the `body_digest` its header carries.

`AuditReader.verify()` does not perform this comparison — that is by
design, and it is why verification needs no keys. The walk comes from the
package's report builder, so the shell never decides what a body digest
means.

body_digest_mismatches.description: Sequence numbers whose body does not hash to the digest their header carries. NON-EMPTY MEANS THE HEADER CHAIN CAN STILL BE INTACT — a swapped body leaves every link verifying, so a consumer that renders chain_ok alone would show a sound file. The answer to 'is what I hold internally consistent?' requires this list to be empty as well.
body_digest_mismatches.title: Body Digest Mismatches

malformed.description: The parser's sentence, when it could not finish.
malformed.title: Malformed

well_formed.description: Whether the container parsed end to end as PALA-1.
well_formed.title: Well Formed

ContainerCheck.title: ContainerCheck

ContinuationModel.description: What a SEGMENT_CONTINUATION declares (inference profile r6, §3.2).

predecessor_head.description: SEG_PREDECESSOR_HEAD, hex — the head the previous segment ended at.
predecessor_head.title: Predecessor Head

prior_root.description: SEG_PRIOR_ROOT, hex — the derived root of every record before this one, as the writer declared it.
prior_root.title: Prior Root

retention_s.description: SEG_RETENTION_S — the declared retention floor in seconds; 0 is none.
retention_s.title: Retention S

ContinuationModel.title: ContinuationModel

DiagnosisModel.description:
What the failure looks like, rather than that there was one.

The pattern is the machine-readable part and a consumer may key visuals
off it. The narrative is the package's own sentence, carried verbatim:
a shell may show a localised sentence beside it, never instead of it, or
the report stops saying what the verifier said.

at_seq.description: Where, when the pattern has a location.
at_seq.title: At Seq

code.description: For record_violation: the violation's code (U24, palimpsests 0.14), the machine field to branch on — `expected` carries the reason as a sentence. Null for every other pattern.
code.title: Code

expected.description: What the verifier expected to find.
expected.title: Expected

pattern.description: The package's pattern, an open vocabulary (a newer verifier may add one; a consumer renders an unknown one with the narrative). As of 0.15: empty_container, not_a_container, truncated_tail, declared_continuation, continuation_contradicts_manifest, prefix_absent, seq_gap, chain_break, record_violation, unanchored_tail, replaced_or_rolled_back.
pattern.title: Pattern

question.description: Which question the diagnosis is about (`Diagnosis.question`, 0.15): the panel its sentence belongs under. Null for a pattern the package does not place — shown, unguided.
question.title: Question

DiagnosisModel.title: DiagnosisModel

HeaderFieldSpan.description:
Where one fixed-header field sits in a record's bytes — the package's
`HEADER_FIELDS` entry, copied (R8).

name.description: The package's name for the field.
name.title: Name

HeaderFieldSpan.title: HeaderFieldSpan

HealthBoot.description: One boot's statistics, as the package computes them (U3).

anchor_gaps_ns.description: Monotonic distance between consecutive anchors in this boot, the package's.
anchor_gaps_ns.title: Anchor Gaps Ns

time_trust.description: Every trust level the boot's records carry.
time_trust.title: Time Trust

uptime_ns.description: By the writer's monotonic clock, within this boot only.
uptime_ns.title: Uptime Ns

HealthBoot.title: HealthBoot

HealthDetail.description: A detail text that recurs among SAFETY records: a pattern, not an episode.
HealthDetail.title: HealthDetail

HealthDrift.description: One boot's drift, as `drift_series` gives it (channel 5).

points.description: How many records the slope was taken over.
points.title: Points

slope_ppm.description: Wall against monotonic, parts per million; null with fewer than two points.
slope_ppm.title: Slope Ppm

time_trusts.description: Every trust level named in the boot.
time_trusts.title: Time Trusts

HealthDrift.title: HealthDrift

HealthKind.description: SAFETY records of one kind, in total and per boot — counted in proved order.
HealthKind.title: HealthKind

HealthLifecycle.description: Whether the boot's writer marked its open and close (profile r8, 0.15).

state.description: `closed`: WRITER_CLOSE is the boot's last record. `stopped`: the writer marked its open, a later boot follows, and no close came — the package's advisory `boot_ended_without_close`. `last_unclosed`: the last boot, open — still being written or stopped for good; the chain cannot tell which. `unmarked`: the writer does not mark its open and close (before profile r8, or turned off).
state.title: State

writer.description: WRITER_OPEN's detail: the writer's name and version.
writer.title: Writer

HealthLifecycle.title: HealthLifecycle

HealthOrigin.description: One stretch of the chain under one origin in force (E-03).

changed.description: What differs from the stretch before, comparing the package's fields: 'model_digest', 'config_digest', 'role', 'loaded', 'unloaded', 'not_stated', 'declared_again'. Empty for the first stretch.
changed.title: Changed

origin.description: The origin in force, as the writer declared it (L3: a claim).

records.description: Records in the stretch, by proved order.
records.title: Records

state.description: 'active', 'unloaded' (a MODEL_UNLOAD ended one) or 'not_stated' (none declared yet).
state.title: State

HealthOrigin.title: HealthOrigin

HealthResponse.description:
Liveness, and the identity of the verifier behind this service.

The verifier identity is part of the liveness answer rather than a
separate endpoint because a verification result is only meaningful
alongside the verifier that produced it. A shell that knows the service is
up but not what it is linked against knows less than it needs.

authenticated.description: Whether the session token gate is enforced. False means the sidecar was started without a token and any local process can reach it — a development affordance, never a supported configuration.
authenticated.title: Authenticated

package.description: The verifier package and version, e.g. 'palimpsests 0.8.0'.
package.title: Package

spec.description: The wire format the linked verifier implements, e.g. 'PALA-1 format_version 1'.
spec.title: Spec

HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse

HealthStep.description: A discontinuity of the writer's clock, as the package classes it (U2).

delta_ns.description: How far the wall clock moved against the monotonic one.
delta_ns.title: Delta Ns

HealthStep.title: HealthStep

HealthWallGap.description: The writer's wall clock from one boot's last record to the next boot's first.

duration_ns.description: Negative when the clock reads earlier after the restart.
duration_ns.title: Duration Ns

HealthWallGap.title: HealthWallGap

KeychainSeedRequest.description: Store a head in the secret store under an account name.

account.description: Account name to store it under.
account.title: Account

KeychainSeedRequest.title: KeychainSeedRequest

KeychainStatus.description: Whether this machine has a usable secret store at all.

available.description: False means there is nowhere on this machine to keep an anchor — a headless box with no Secret Service, a session without credentials, or the keyring extra not installed. Distinct from 'your anchor was not found', and a UI that conflates the two sends the operator to look for a value that could never have been read.
available.title: Available

detail.description: What to do about it, when there is something to do.
detail.title: Detail

KeychainStatus.title: KeychainStatus

ManifestReadingModel.description:
The segments manifest a verdict consulted (U17, palimpsests 0.13).

A segment whose first record declares a continuation is diagnosed
against `<stem>.segments.json` beside it. That second file is part of
what the verdict is about, so it is named and fingerprinted here, and
the session refuses to answer once either file has changed.

detail.description: The package's reason, when the status is not plain. Verbatim.
detail.title: Detail

path.description: The manifest looked for; null when there was no path to derive it from (the file is not named <stem>.<digits>).
path.title: Path

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the bytes the package read and judged; null when no file was read.
sha256.title: Sha256

status.description: matches / contradicts / declared_only — as the diagnosis used it.
status.title: Status

ManifestReadingModel.title: ManifestReadingModel

NamedValue.description:
A header enum value, with the package's name for it.

Both halves travel. The name is what a person reads; the number is what
survives a name table changing and what can be checked against the
specification. `name` is null when this verifier build has no name for
the value — which is a real answer, and better than a label invented to
fill the gap.

name.description: The package's name, or null if this build does not know it.
name.title: Name

NamedValue.title: NamedValue

NearestRecord.description:
The record nearest an instant, by the writer's clock (C-09c).

Every field that qualifies the answer travels with it. "Nearest to
22:41" is decided by `wall_clock_ns`, a Recorded claim, so the answer is
a statement about the writer's clock, never about when something
happened.

asked_ns.description: The instant asked about, as received.
asked_ns.title: Asked Ns

basis.description: Always 'recorded'. Carried rather than implied, so no consumer can present this as a proved position in the history.
basis.title: Basis

boot_clock_stepped.description: Whether the package's step catalogue reports a clock step in this record's boot — a stepped boot measures two clocks.
boot_clock_stepped.title: Boot Clock Stepped

delta_ns.description: wall_clock_ns − asked_ns. Signed: negative means the record's clock reads before the instant asked about.
delta_ns.title: Delta Ns

equally_near.description: How many OTHER records sit at exactly the same distance. Ties resolve to the lowest seq; the count makes that choice visible rather than silent.
equally_near.title: Equally Near

time_trust.description: The writer's own status for its clock at that record.

wall_follows_seq.description: Whether the writer's clock is non-decreasing along proved order across the file. FALSE MEANS 'NEAREST' IS A STATEMENT ABOUT THE CLOCK ONLY: records far apart in the chain can sit next to each other in wall time, and a UI must say so.
wall_follows_seq.title: Wall Follows Seq

NearestRecord.title: NearestRecord

OriginModel.description:
What was running when a record was written.

Every field is a **Recorded** claim: the writer declared it, and nothing
in the chain proves the process was actually running that model. The
digests let a reader compare against an artifact they hold; they do not
establish what produced the records.

config_digest.description: Hex digest of the configuration as the writer declared it.
config_digest.title: Config Digest

detail.description: Free text the writer attached, when it attached any.
detail.title: Detail

model_digest.description: Hex digest of the model as the writer declared it.
model_digest.title: Model Digest

since_seq.description: The record that declared this origin. A reader can jump to it and see the declaration rather than take this on trust — the same reason every other claim here names its source.
since_seq.title: Since Seq

OriginModel.title: OriginModel

OriginState.description:
What F9 needs said about a record's origin — three states, not
the two `AuditReader.origin_at()` alone can tell apart.

`origin_at()` returns null for two different facts: nothing has
been declared yet, and something was declared and then explicitly
unloaded (a MODEL_UNLOAD record) — both leave its running state at
null. `unloaded_at()` (U11, released 0.11.0) is the package's own
way to tell them apart, additive to `origin_at()` rather than a
change to it.

origin.description: The declared origin, present only when state is 'active'.

state.description: One of: active, unloaded, not_stated. 'active' means a model is declared running — see `origin` below. 'unloaded' means one was declared and then explicitly ended by a MODEL_UNLOAD. 'not_stated' means nothing has been declared at or before this record at all.
state.title: State

OriginState.title: OriginState

RecordBytesView.description:
One record as the file holds it, with the package's maps of it (C-06d).

The bytes are the package's `record_bytes_at`, never re-encoded. Every
span is the package's; a byte no span covers is shown, unnamed.

body_hex.description: The body as stored — ciphertext for an encrypted one — up to body_shown bytes, lowercase hex. The body starts where the header ends.
body_hex.title: Body Hex

body_len.description: The stored body's whole length in bytes.
body_len.title: Body Len

body_shown.description: How many of the body's bytes body_hex carries. Less than body_len means the rest was not sent, never that it is absent.
body_shown.title: Body Shown

body_tlvs.description: The body's TLVs, in order. Null when the package gives no TLV layout for this body: a header it rejects, an encrypted body, an empty or a malformed one. Offsets may lie past body_shown.
body_tlvs.title: Body Tlvs

header_fields.description: The fixed header's fields. Null when the package does not accept this header — an unknown format version among the cases — since the map would then name a layout this record may not have.
header_fields.title: Header Fields

header_hex.description: The fixed header and its TLVs as stored, lowercase hex.
header_hex.title: Header Hex

header_tlvs.description: The header's TLVs, in order; null exactly when header_fields is.
header_tlvs.title: Header Tlvs

offset.description: Where the record starts in the file, in bytes.
offset.title: Offset

RecordBytesView.title: RecordBytesView

RecordHealthView.description:
Record health (E-03, F12): the record as an artefact, never its content.

Every figure is the package's detection, copied, or a count of it. No
threshold is applied and nothing is called anomalous; advisory, and it
never touches the verdict.

drift.description: Per boot, in chain order: the package's `drift_series`, copied.
drift.title: Drift

drift_note.description: The clock the drift figures are measured on.
drift_note.title: Drift Note

origins.description: SAFETY records against the origin in force, one entry per stretch of the chain between origin changes, in chain order — a count, never an interpretation.
origins.title: Origins

recurring_details.description: Details seen more than once, most frequent first, at most twenty.
recurring_details.title: Recurring Details

RecordHealthView.title: RecordHealthView

RecordPage.description:
A window onto the records.

Paginated because a chain has no bound: a container from a busy
deployment can hold millions of records, and an endpoint that serialised
all of them would fail in the situation where the tool is most needed.

has_more.description: Whether records remain past this window. Stated rather than left to be inferred from len(records) == limit, which is ambiguous when a window ends exactly on the last record.
has_more.title: Has More

limit.description: Most records this window would return.
limit.title: Limit

offset.description: First sequence number this window could include.
offset.title: Offset

total.description: Records that MATCHED THE FILTERS, not records in the file. With no filters the two are the same, which is why this field could quietly say the wrong thing once filters existed: a total counting everything would print '3 of 40000' above three rows that are the only three there are.
total.title: Total

unsearched.description: With a text filter: how many records passed every other filter but have an encrypted body, so their detail could not be searched. Null when no text was asked for. A non-zero value means 'no match' is not the whole answer.
unsearched.title: Unsearched

RecordPage.title: RecordPage

RecordView.description:
One record, as structure rather than as content.

Header fields and the shape of the body. What is *inside* a record is a
separate view with its own decisions about keys and redaction.

ack_latency_ns.description: For an acknowledged INCIDENT_CANDIDATE: wall_clock(ack) − wall_clock(candidate), a RECORDED figure — two claims of the writer's clock subtracted, never proved. Computed only when both records are in the same boot: across a restart the clock may have been set, and a number would span a period nobody observed. acknowledged_by non-null with this null means exactly that — a cross-boot pair. Can be negative, when the writer's clock went backwards; shown as it is rather than clamped.
ack_latency_ns.title: Ack Latency Ns

acknowledged.description: For an INCIDENT_CANDIDATE: whether a hash-verified OVERSIGHT_ACK names it (U13, released 0.11.0). Null for every other kind — 'not acknowledged' and 'not the kind of record that gets acknowledged' are different facts, and collapsing them to false would claim something about a record that never made the claim. Which ack is `acknowledged_by`.
acknowledged.title: Acknowledged

acknowledged_by.description: For an INCIDENT_CANDIDATE: the seq of the OVERSIGHT_ACK that acknowledges it, from the package's hash-verified resolution (acknowledged_candidates(), 0.12.0). Null when not acknowledged, and for every other kind. An ack whose reference does not verify never appears here; the advisory channel names it instead.
acknowledged_by.title: Acknowledged By

acknowledges.description: For an OVERSIGHT_ACK: the seq of the candidate it verifiably acknowledges — the same resolution read backwards. Null for an ack whose reference does not verify, which must not look like it acknowledges anything, and for every other kind.
acknowledges.title: Acknowledges

body_tlv_types.description: TLV types present in the body, or null when this view has none to show — a record type with no body, an encrypted body, or one this build cannot parse. Distinct from [], which would mean a decoded body containing nothing.
body_tlv_types.title: Body Tlv Types

continuation.description: On a SEGMENT_CONTINUATION (kind 11): what the writer declared at the cut, as the package decodes it. Null on every other record, and on a kind-11 record that is not well formed (the advisory channel reports that). A declaration, never evidence that the records it describes exist.

detail.description: EVT_DETAIL, decoded generically for any record type that carries one — EVENT and SAFETY bodies, the same scope `kind` already has (U12, released 0.11.0). Null when the record carries no detail at all, never an empty string.
detail.title: Detail

disposition.description: For an OVERSIGHT_ACK: the disposition the writer recorded, with the package's name for it (e.g. DISMISSED). Null for every record that carries none.

index.description: Position of this record within THIS FILE, zero-based. Distinct from seq, which a rotated or segmented chain does not start at zero and does not number contiguously across a gap — index always does, because it counts what this file actually holds.
index.title: Index

key_id.description: Encryption key identifier, or null when the body is not encrypted.
key_id.title: Key Id

kind.description: Raw kind, for types that carry one.
kind.title: Kind

kind_name.description: The package's name for the kind. Null where the record type has no kind at all — GENESIS, BOOT and ANCHOR do not — which is not the same as a kind this build cannot name.
kind_name.title: Kind Name

monotonic_ns.description: Monotonic clock. Comparable only within one boot.
monotonic_ns.title: Monotonic Ns

operator_id.description: For an OVERSIGHT_ACK: the operator id the writer recorded, hex. Pseudonymous by design (16 bytes the writer chose); this application never resolves it to a person. Null for every record that carries none.
operator_id.title: Operator Id

outcome.description: On a TOOL_RESULT: the outcome the writer recorded (EVT_OUTCOME), with the package's name — 'ok', 'error', 'timeout', 'cancelled', or 'unobserved' (r6: the result returned and the recording vantage could not observe whether it failed). 'ok' IS A RETURN, NOT A CONFIRMED EFFECT (profile note 5), and a reader cannot treat it as 'the tool did not fail'. Null on every other record, and on a result missing the tag; name null for a value this build cannot interpret.

parent_span_id.description: The enclosing span, when there is one.
parent_span_id.title: Parent Span Id

prev_hash.description: Hex hash of the predecessor's header, or null for a record declaring it has none. PALA-1 spells 'no predecessor' as thirty-two zero bytes — the GENESIS convention (§4.2: 'no predecessor' and 'predecessor removed' must be distinguishable, which is the entire reason GENESIS is a type) — so this field reports null rather than a hash of all zeros, the same choice span_id already makes for 'no span'. This is the record's OWN CLAIM about its predecessor, unverified here: whether it actually matches the predecessor's hash is a chain-link fact, not a structural one, and belongs to /verify, not to this view.
prev_hash.title: Prev Hash

prev_seq.description: The seq of the record prev_hash names, or null when there is none in this file. NOT seq - 1: the hash chain links by position in this container (the record immediately before this one), never by seq value, and a seq gap is a wholly independent fact — a rotated or segmented chain can have both at once. Null at the first record in this file, whether that is GENESIS's own declared zero predecessor or a segment's first record naming a predecessor outside this container: either way, nothing here to jump to.
prev_seq.title: Prev Seq

record_hash.description: This record's own hex hash (U10, palimpsests 0.11.0) — the SHA-256 the package computes over the header bytes. Always present, even for a record whose header did not otherwise decode: the hash is over the raw bytes, which the chain check hashes regardless of whether this view could read their fields.
record_hash.title: Record Hash

recurrence_count.description: How many SAFETY records in this container carry this exact detail text, this one included (F8: 'detail text and a recurrence count for identical details'). Scoped to SAFETY the way `acknowledged` is scoped to INCIDENT_CANDIDATE: null for a non-SAFETY record (not applicable) and for a SAFETY record with no detail (nothing to count) — never 0, since a detail that exists recurs at least once, itself.
recurrence_count.title: Recurrence Count

reports_refused.description: On a REPORTS_REFUSED (kind 14, profile r9): the route and its four counts as the package decodes them. Null on every other record and on one that is not well formed.

shred.description: On a KEY_SHRED: its erasure note as the package decodes it (`decode_shred`). A declaration; whether its targets exist and carried the key is `shredded_by` and the advisories. Null elsewhere.

shredded_by.description: Seq of the KEY_SHRED that shreds this record, resolved in the chain and key_id-matched (U15, released 0.11.0), or null when it is not currently shredded. A KEY_SHRED's own target_seqs can name any record, so no kind is excluded structurally — null here means 'not shredded', not 'not shreddable'.
shredded_by.title: Shredded By

source.description: On a TOOL_CALL or TOOL_RESULT: how the serving layer learned of it (EVT_SOURCE, inference profile r5), with the package's name — 'parsed-from-wire', the runtime's own observation of a loop it mediated, or 'reported-by-client', the client's assertion faithfully recorded. The chain proves a reported call was reported, what it digested and when — NEVER THAT THE TOOL ACTUALLY RAN. An evidence-quality mark, never a trust upgrade. Null on every other record, where the mark has no meaning; name null for a value this build cannot interpret.

span_id.description: Hex span identifier, or null when the record is in no span. PALA-1 spells that as sixteen zero bytes; this field reports null rather than a span named 00000000…
span_id.title: Span Id

type_name.description: The package's name for the type, or null if unknown to this build.
type_name.title: Type Name

wall_clock_ns.description: The writer's wall clock. A Recorded claim, qualified by time_trust.
wall_clock_ns.title: Wall Clock Ns

ReportResponse.description:
The package's verification report, passed through whole (D-01).

Auditor does not build reports (ADR-0001): `build_report` does, and its
verdict comes from `derive_verdict`, the package's one verdict rule. This
response carries the report as the package returned it, and the exact
JSON text the package serialised, so a copy is the package's bytes.

format.description: The report's own format id, e.g. 'pala-verification-report/2' (palimpsests 0.15).
format.title: Format

html_text.description: The same report as the package renders it (`render_html`, channel 2 since palimpsests 0.14): one self-contained HTML page — no script, no link, no outbound URL. Built from the same report object, never by this application.
html_text.title: Html Text

json_text.description: The report as the package serialised it (`to_json_bytes`), UTF-8. What a copy or an export carries.
json_text.title: Json Text

report.description: The report object, exactly as `build_report` returned it.
report.title: Report

session_id.description: The session this report is about.
session_id.title: Session Id

subject_sha256.description: Digest of the file as opened. Repeated beside the report so the two cannot be separated.
subject_sha256.title: Subject Sha256

verdict.description: The report's verdict as the package derived it (`derive_verdict`): 'sound', 'partial', 'empty' (report /2) or 'violation'. Copied from the report, never re-derived here.
verdict.title: Verdict

ReportResponse.title: ReportResponse

Two answers, as the package keeps them: consistent (everything present
holds and agrees with the manifest) and complete (that, with nothing
listed missing, starting at a GENESIS). Retention makes a set

Timeline.description:
Record density along one axis, and what breaks the ruler.

**Two axes, and they are not interchangeable (L3).** `seq` is proved
order: the hash chain establishes it and nothing can reorder it. `wall`
is the writer's clock — a recorded claim, qualified by `time_trust`.

align.description: Null for uniform buckets, 'day' when each bucket is one UTC calendar day. A CONSUMER RENDERING DATES MUST CHECK THIS: a date printed from a uniform bucket's start is a date the records inside it may not have happened on, because such a bucket straddles midnight.
align.title: Align

basis.description: 'proved' for the seq axis, 'recorded' for the wall axis. Carried as its own field rather than left to be derived from `axis`, so a consumer cannot label a wall chart 'proved' by reading the wrong one.
basis.title: Basis

boot_boundaries.description: Reported apart from the series, because they are axis breaks.
boot_boundaries.title: Boot Boundaries

buckets.description: Equal-width intervals covering the range, empty ones included. How many there are depends on `align`: without it the range is divided into at most the number requested; with 'day' each is one calendar day and the count is however many days the chain spans.
buckets.title: Buckets

start.description: Where the first bucket begins. Equal to the lowest position on this axis for uniform buckets, and THE UTC MIDNIGHT AT OR BEFORE IT when align='day' — the first day is a whole day even when the chain starts in the middle of one.
start.title: Start

steps.description: Clock steps the package detected, with where and how far.
steps.title: Steps

time_trust_values.description: Every clock-trust level the records carry. The watermark for a wall-time view: it says whose clock this is, and how much the writer claimed for it.
time_trust_values.title: Time Trust Values

wall_follows_seq.description: Whether wall_clock_ns is non-decreasing along proved order. FALSE MEANS THE WALL AXIS REORDERS RECORDS relative to the chain, and a UI showing that axis must say so.
wall_follows_seq.title: Wall Follows Seq

wall_gaps.description: The intervals between boots, where the ruler does not apply.
wall_gaps.title: Wall Gaps

Timeline.title: Timeline

TimelineBucket.description:
One interval of the axis, and what fell inside it.

Present even when empty. An empty stretch is a fact about the chain —
the quiet week, the gap between boots — and a series that omitted empty
buckets would draw a dense chain out of a sparse one.

anchor.description: How many of them are ANCHOR records.
anchor.title: Anchor

end.description: Last position in this bucket, inclusive.
end.title: End

safety.description: How many of them are SAFETY records.
safety.title: Safety

start.description: First position in this bucket, inclusive.
start.title: Start

stepped.description: Whether the writer's clock stepped inside this bucket. On the wall axis a stepped bucket is measuring two different clocks, so its width means nothing — a UI must mark it rather than draw it like the others.
stepped.title: Stepped

TimelineBucket.title: TimelineBucket

TlvSpan.description: One TLV's value, where the package says it sits (U31).

value_offset.description: Where the VALUE starts, from the record's first byte. The bytes that introduce it are not given a span of their own: the package names the value, and nothing here works out the rest.
value_offset.title: Value Offset

VerificationResponse.description:
The verifier's answer, passed through rather than summarised.

There is deliberately no single "valid" field. The three questions have
three separate answers, one of which can be "not asked", and any field
that collapsed them would be the shell deciding what a verdict means.

anchor.description: The source that answered, or null when none did. A completeness answer is worth exactly as much as the anchor behind it, so the two are never separated.

anchor_attempts.description: Every source consulted, in order, including those that were absent or failed. The answering source alone would let a UI present it as 'the' anchor while silently skipping a source the operator believed was authoritative.
anchor_attempts.title: Anchor Attempts

consistent.description: Question one in the package's one answer (`is_consistent()`, 0.15): the header chain links, the container walks to its end, and every body matches its digest — `consistency.ok` in `pala verify --json`, `consistent` in the export and the bundle. True for a file with no records, which is not a log found intact.
consistent.title: Consistent

container.description: The body-digest walk. Required rather than optional: a response that could omit it would let a consumer answer question one from the header chain alone.

manifest.description: The second file this verdict rests on, when there is one: the segments manifest a continuation diagnosis was decided against. Null when the verdict consulted no manifest.

session_id.description: The session this answer is about.
session_id.title: Session Id

subject_sha256.description: Digest of the file this answer describes. Repeated here so a verification result cannot be separated from its subject.
subject_sha256.title: Subject Sha256

verifier.description: Package and wire format behind it.
verifier.title: Verifier

witness.description: Where this check went in the local witness log (E-05): its entry, or why none was written. Null only for a response built without a log.

VerificationResponse.title: VerificationResponse

WallGap.description:
The wall-clock distance between one boot's end and the next one's start.

Reported with both ends so a consumer can hatch the interval and **remove
the ruler inside it**: the clock is unverifiable while the system is
down, which is a statement about the gap rather than about the records
on either side.

duration_ns.description: to_wall_ns minus from_wall_ns. CAN BE NEGATIVE — that means the writer's clock moved backwards across the boundary, which the ruler cannot represent and a UI must not hide.
duration_ns.title: Duration Ns

from_wall_ns.description: Wall clock at the earlier boot's last record.
from_wall_ns.title: From Wall Ns

to_wall_ns.description: Wall clock at the later boot's first record.
to_wall_ns.title: To Wall Ns

WallGap.title: WallGap

get.description:
Whether this machine can keep an anchor at all.

Asked before the operator configures a keychain profile, so the UI
can say "this machine has nowhere to keep one" rather than letting
them configure a source that will report absent forever.

put.description:
Store a head in the secret store.

This writes, and the read-only rule still holds: the target is
Auditor's own anchor store, never an audited container. The rule is
about not touching evidence, not about never writing a byte.

It exists so an operator can seed an anchor from the application
rather than from a shell one-liner they have to get exactly right —
and a head seeded with a typo persists, so getting it right matters
more here than anywhere else.

get.description: Every profile this sidecar knows, including the empty one.

schema.title: Response List Profiles Anchors Profiles Get

put.description:
Define or replace a profile.

The body's `name` is ignored in favour of the path, so a profile
cannot be defined under one name and answer to another.

get.description:
Where profiles are kept, and why they cannot be changed if they cannot.

Asked by the window's profile editor, so a file that could not be
read is said once, with its path, rather than as a refusal on every
save.

Liveness probe, and the identity triple the UI displays.

The verifier version is reported because a verification result is only
meaningful alongside the verifier that produced it.

post.description:
A segmented chain, verified as a set (§22.1, U18).

Stateless: the manifest and every segment are read for this answer
and nothing is kept, so asking again reads the files as they are
now. A segment is browsed by opening it as its own session.

422 when the file is not a `pala-segments/1` manifest or cannot be
read, with the reason; everything else — absent, altered or
mismatched segments — is an answer.

Open a container and return what it is.

Deliberately says nothing about whether the chain verifies. Identity
and structure are established first, and separately: a reader of a
report must be able to confirm they hold the same artifact the check
ran against, whether or not that check passed.

get.description:
The boots in this container, with their statistics.

Browsing is separate from verifying, and answers no question about
soundness. A chain that fails verification is still browsed — half
the job is inspecting evidence that did not pass.

schema.title: Response Session Boots Session  Session Id  Boots Get

get.description:
An evidence bundle for a selection of this session's records (E-01).

`assemble_bundle` (channel 4) writes the tar into a directory of the
sidecar's own; it is sent, then removed. The desktop shell streams it
into the file the user chose, as it does the export — the webview
never holds it.

**Bounded.** A bundle carries each record and its proof path, so it
outgrows its source (R12): at most 100,000 records per bundle; 422
for more, for a range outside the chain or backwards, and for a file
with no records. 409 if the file changed, 404 for an unknown profile.

A prefix-consistency proof between two counts of this chain (E-07).

The package's `consistency_proof` (channel 3): the first `first`
records are a prefix of the first `second`, over the derived §4.3
root of record hashes. Derived and unsigned: it proves two roots are
consistent, never where a root came from. 422 for counts outside
1 ≤ first ≤ second ≤ records; 409 if the file changed.

post.description:
A proof someone holds, checked against this chain (E-07).

The document is read from `path` — a file the desktop shell's dialog
chose — and checked three ways, kept apart: whether its path connects
its two roots, and whether this chain's own roots at its two counts
are the roots it names. 422 when the file cannot be read or is not a
`pala-consistency-proof/1`.

get.description:
The package's record export for this session, streamed (D-06).

`export_jsonl` writes it (channel 2 since 0.14.1); this route only
carries the lines out as they are written, so a 1M-record chain is
never held whole in memory. The desktop shell reads this stream
straight into the file the user chose — the webview never holds it.

The export reads no anchor, and its summary says so
(`completeness_checked: false`): `consistent: true` is about the
records present, never about records missing from the end.

409 if the file changed since the session opened; 422 for a range
whose start is after its end — an empty range would be an answer to
a question nobody meant to ask.

The record nearest an instant by the writer's clock (C-09c).

Always answered with the qualifiers attached — `basis`,
`time_trust`, `wall_follows_seq`, `boot_clock_stepped`,
`equally_near` — because the answer is a statement about a
Recorded clock and must not travel without saying so.

get.description:
What was running when a record was written — three states.

**`state` carries the distinction a bare null could not.**
`origin_at()` alone returns null for two different facts:
nothing has been declared yet ("not_stated"), and something was
declared and then explicitly ended by a MODEL_UNLOAD
("unloaded") — both left its running state at null before U11
(released 0.11.0) added `unloaded_at()` to tell them apart. A UI
must render each as its own sentence, never as one empty card
that reads as "nothing was running" regardless of which is true.

Always 200. The question is always answered; `state` says which
answer it is, `origin` carries the declared fields only when
`state` is `"active"`.

parameters.description: The record to ask about. Required rather than defaulted: origin changes along a chain, so an unasked-for default would answer a different question than the caller meant.
parameters.name: seq

schema.description: The record to ask about. Required rather than defaulted: origin changes along a chain, so an unasked-for default would answer a different question than the caller meant.

get.description:
Record health (E-03, F12): clock steps, boot and anchor cadence,
spans, the gaps between boots, SAFETY by kind and boot, recurring
details. The package's detection, counted here; advisory.

One record by sequence number.

404 when the file holds no such record. A segment covering records
400–900 legitimately has no record 12, and saying so is different
from saying the session is unknown — which the caller can tell apart
because that 404 names the session instead.

One record's bytes as the file holds them, and where the package

The package's verification report for this session (D-01).

Built by `build_report`, never here; built once per profile, because
a second build would carry a second `checked_at` — a different
attestation of the same check. The same refusals as /verify: 409 if
the file changed, 404 for an unknown profile, 422 for an anchor kind
this build does not implement.

parameters.name: health

schema.title: Health

get.description:
Every SAFETY record — F8's first-class list, not a filter.

No caller-adjustable `limit`, unlike `/records`. This answer is
cached for the life of the session the same way boots and spans
are — one question, one answer — and a caller-visible limit would
have needed a cache keyed by it, the exact class of bug the
`Session` docstring documents avoiding elsewhere: a second caller
asking with a different limit would silently receive the first
caller's cached answer at the first caller's limit.

`ChainHandle.safety` still bounds the response internally, purely
defensively, at a size no caller chooses.

The same `RecordPage` shape `/records` returns, reused rather than
given one of its own: `total` counts every SAFETY record that
exists, which can exceed the internal cap on an unusually large
chain, and `has_more` says so rather than leaving it to be
inferred from a length that matches the cap by coincidence.

Detail text and its recurrence count are on in full (C-07b,
U12). So is the oversight loop (C-07c): which ack acknowledged
a candidate, the candidate an ack verifiably acknowledges, the
ack's operator and disposition, and — within one boot only — the
latency between them by the writer's clock.

post.description:
A SCITT Signed Statement about this chain, checked (E-06).

The statement and the issuer's public key are read from the two
files the desktop shell's dialogs chose, and handed to the package's
`verify_statement` (channel 8) with this chain's head at the
statement's `last_seq` and this session's reader. A statement the
package refuses is an answer — `accepted` false, with its code and
sentence — not an error. 422 when a file cannot be read, is too
large to be one, or the key is not a public key; 409 if the chain
changed.

Displayed, never minted: Auditor signs and registers nothing. And it
does not check receipts — that is the transparency service's protocol.

get.description:
The verifier's answer about this session's container.

Re-checks the file digest first. A verdict about bytes that have since
changed is worse than no verdict, because it looks like one.

Note what this endpoint does NOT return: a single "valid" field. The
three questions have three separate answers, one of which can be "not
asked", and collapsing them here would be the shell deciding what a
verdict means — which is the one thing ADR-0001 exists to prevent.

post.description:
Watch a file as it is written (F15), through the package's
`TailingReader` (channel 9, provisional in 0.15).

Not a session: a session is pinned to the bytes it opened, and a
watched file grows. The watch reports what happens at the tail and
answers the batch questions over what it has verified, on request.
At most `MAX_WATCHES` at once; 422 for a path that is not a file,
404 for an unknown profile.

delete.description: Stop watching and forget the watch. The file is never touched.

What happened at the tail since `after`, and the watch's state.

Long-polled: with nothing new and the watch live, the answer waits up
to `wait` seconds. Only the latest events are kept; `dropped` says how
many a reader that fell behind did not see.

get.description:
The batch verification over the records verified so far.

`TailingReader.snapshot()` — the package's batch path, so live and
after the fact agree. It re-verifies every record held on each call
(R17), so it is asked for, not polled. Only what that verification
holds is returned: no container walk and no `is_consistent()` — a
torn tail still being written is `pending`, not a finding. For those,
stop and open the file.

The local witness log: whether it links, and its last entries (E-05).

The check walks the whole log, every time it is asked; nothing is
remembered between calls, because the file is the user's and can
change between them.
